newsitem.title: ITALY: Any Italy mini-budget no more than 1 pct GDP - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Any Italy mini-budget no more than 1 pct GDP - Dini.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said in an interview published on Friday that if Italy needed to pass a mini-budget, he expected it to amount to no more than one percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
"If we need to make an additional correction, it will very probably not be much more than one percentage point of GDP," he told the Rome newspaper Il Tempo in an interview.
Dini's remarks, which suggested an eventual mini-budget in the order of 19-20 billion lire ($11.6-12.3 million), were the first official comment on the possible size of any such package.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has already said the decision on whether to pass a mini-budget will be made in late February or early March, when official state accounts are published.

He has also said that any mini-budget will consist entirely of spending cuts and will include no new tax hikes. The 1997 austerity budget, designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire off this year's deficit, contains unpopular tax rises.

Analysts see no alternative to a mini-budget to help plug a hole in state accounts caused by an overshoot in the 1996 public sector deficit borrowing requirement and keep Italy's finances on course for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). ($1=1,634)
